upstream.base_commit_subject: Standardize on 1 MiB default chunk size across all libraries (#1659)
upstream.archive_notes: git archive of the base commit with all 456 Git-LFS pointer files replaced by their real content (conformance corpus, rust test fixtures, testdata); no .git, no solution, no hidden tests. Deterministic tar (uid/gid 0, mtime = commit time).

feature.title: rust cli: Bring recover command to parity
feature.author: amacneil (authored with a Cursor background agent per the PR body)
feature.composition: single PR; #1646 (cat parity) not composed because #1647 alone is ~968 non-test code lines with a dozen interacting requirements (streaming, codec selection, exit codes, per-kind loss accounting, corrupt-chunk policy, remote streaming, record-length bound, stdout discipline)

oracle.reference: Go mcap CLI (go/cli/mcap) and Go conformance reader (go/conformance/test-read-conformance) built from the same base commit with golang:1.22.12; Go `recover -a` output dumped record-by-record and compared to the Rust output dumped by the same reader; Go `mcap doctor` validates every Rust output; corpus expectations cross-checked against tests/conformance/data/*.json at image build (selfcheck.py)
differential_classes: valid corpus (416) + multi-chunk zstd/uncompressed fixtures + demo + lz4/zstd variants of 5 message-bearing files produced by Go filter (zstd_chunk_with_padding.mcap references an undefined channel and is tested as a missing-channel case instead)

truncation at every record boundary and several interior offsets of 40 files (the Data End body-absent offset is excluded: upstream LinearReader reports a clean EOF there); truncation inside an Attachment is compared against Go on the prefix before it (Go keeps a CRC-less attachment)
undecodable chunk payload (unsupported codec string, garbage compressed frame) -> stop
removed loose schema/channel -> dependents dropped; messages for a never-defined channel (zstd_chunk_with_padding.mcap) dropped
missing summary/footer/DataEnd, trailing garbage, absurd record lengths, empty/garbage files
preserve codec selection on constructed mixes
oracle.upstream_tests: rust/mcap integration tests restored from pristine (17 tests, exact count); rust/cli inline unit tests must pass (agent-authored, count recorded only)

contamination.notes: Merged 2026-06-01. The gold patch is AI-assisted upstream code; the task instruction is written from the behavioral contract (PR body + README divergences) and the hidden harness tests behaviors the PR's own 2 cli-conformance cases do not cover. Agent container keeps public network on the Docker backend (allowlist unsupported there); the merged PR diff is fetchable in principle. Prefer a backend with network_allowlist or review trajectories for upstream lookups.

horizon.proxy: 5 code files, ~968 non-test lines added / 345 removed, 2 subsystems (CLI command + input plumbing) plus exit-code plumbing through main/dispatch; 12 interacting requirements

evidence: rust/cli/README.md at base: recover marked partial, 'Go-parity gaps remain around raw chunk passthrough behavior'
AGENTS.md design principle: bounded memory when reading; the base recover buffers stdin fully

derivability.assertion: exit 0 on clean recovery, 3 on lossy, 1 on hard failure / nothing recovered; 'nonzero' for removed flag
derivability.instruction_ref: Exit codes table; Command surface (--always-decode-chunk removed)

derivability.assertion: stderr contains exactly the line 'Recovered N message(s), M attachment(s), and K metadata record(s).' with naive pluralization, counts from the Go-derived expected stream
derivability.instruction_ref: Standard error, summary line and pluralization examples

derivability.assertion: a line starting 'Recovery was lossy:' iff exit 3
stdout empty when -o given; MCAP bytes on stdout otherwise (stdout pipe mode)
output record stream (schemas by id, channels by id, ordered messages, attachments, metadata) equals Go recover -a on valid and truncated inputs
derivability.instruction_ref: Intentional divergences last paragraph; Recovery semantics 6-7

derivability.assertion: mcap-go doctor accepts every output, including stdout-pipe outputs
output header profile/library equal the input header's
unparsable header -> exit 3, output profile empty, all other records recovered

truncation inside any record (incl. index records and the Data End length/body bytes other than the exact opcode+length boundary, which the upstream reader treats as EOF and is not tested) -> exit 3 with everything before it; at a record boundary -> exit 0; inside the first record or magic -> exit 1; after DataEnd -> exit 0 full
corrupted chunk CRC -> exit 0, full content
unsupported compression string / garbage compressed frame -> chunk discarded, scan stops, exit 3, content = everything before the chunk
unparsable schema/channel/message/metadata/attachment top-level body -> discarded, scan continues, exit 3, dependents dropped
removed loose channel -> its messages dropped; removed schema -> channel and messages dropped; messages whose channel is never defined -> dropped; exit 3
unknown/private opcode records (top-level and in-chunk) skipped, exit 0
missing summary / footer / DataEnd or trailing garbage -> exit 0 full recovery
record length 2^64-1 (chunk_not_closed.mcap, synthetic) -> scan stops, exit 3, header-only output
empty file, magic only, short magic, non-MCAP -> exit 1
derivability.instruction_ref: Exit codes (no complete record); Recovery semantics 10

derivability.assertion: preserve: chunk-first input keeps the chunk codec; message/attachment/private-first input -> uncompressed chunks; unchunked input -> uncompressed
explicit --compression none|zstd|lz4 -> all output chunks use it
--chunk-size 4096 on the 413-chunk fixture (~104 KiB of message payload) yields >= 20 output chunks and --chunk-size 1024 yields >= 50 (Rust writer: 32 / 110)
--compression snappy -> exit 1 and stderr names preserve, none, zstd, lz4
recover --help exits 0 with non-empty stdout; missing input or unwritable output -> exit 1
stdin input behaves like a file; loopback http URL with --allow-remote-scan behaves like a file; without the flag -> exit 1
derivability.instruction_ref: Command surface, FILE and Remote inputs

derivability.assertion: 512 MiB input from path and from stdin: exit 0, 2048 messages with correct payload digest, peak RssAnon < 256 MiB
cargo test -p mcap integration tests (17) pass; cargo test -p mcap-cli passes
sources contain no reference to external executables / verifier paths; no symlinks

not_tested_but_specified: record inside a chunk fails to parse -> chunk stops the scan (upstream behavior, stated in rule 5, not exercised because agents may reasonably skip-and-continue and the corpus has no such fixture)
attachment CRC mismatch (upstream discards the attachment; documented upstream as a pre-1.0 gap, deliberately not enshrined)
exact wording of warnings and of the 'Recovery was lossy:' detail
